subject: AI & Agents
title: Cross-Validation: Testing Without Waste
description: A quick, practical guide to Cross-Validation: Testing Without Waste.

hook.text: You only have 1,000 examples. Holding out 200 for testing wastes 20% of your precious data.

buildup.text: Cross-validation splits data into k folds, trains on k-1, and tests on the remaining fold.

discovery.text: Rotate through all folds so every example gets to be in the test set exactly once.

twist.text: It's slower — you train k models instead of one. But the evaluation is far more reliable.

climax.text: Five-fold cross-validation is the standard for reporting results in machine learning research.

punchline.text: Use all your data for training AND testing. Just not at the same time.

quiz.question: What is the benefit of cross-validation?
options: It uses all data for both training and testing
It eliminates the need for test data

details.summary: Cross-validation rotates portions of data between training and testing, ensuring every example gets used for both. It provides more reliable performance estimates than a single train-test split, especially with limited data.
details.whyItMatters: A single test set might give misleading results by chance. Cross-validation produces robust performance estimates that better predict real-world behavior, critical when data is scarce.
takeaways: Data is split into folds that rotate between training and testing
Every example serves as both training and test data across folds
It provides more reliable estimates than a single split

faq.question: How does k-fold cross-validation work?
faq.answer: Data is split into k equal parts. The model trains on k-1 parts and tests on the remaining one. This rotates k times so each part serves as the test set once. Results are averaged across all folds.

faq.question: What value of k is commonly used?
faq.answer: k=5 or k=10 are most common, balancing computational cost with estimate reliability. With very small datasets, leave-one-out cross-validation uses k equal to the number of examples for maximum data usage.
